commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.name: mcp-builder
commands.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (user)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: startup-hook-skill

commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. commands.description: Suite of tools for creating elaborate, multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts using modern frontend web technologies (React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui). commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (user)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Both errors in `client/src/pages/UserDashboard.tsx` are fixed at the type level.

**What was actually wrong**

1. **TS2322 (line 474)** — `ApiKeyCard` hand-declared its prop shape as
   `{ id: number; keyPrefix: string; name: string | null; isActive: boolean; createdAt: Date; lastUsedAt: Date | null }`,
   but `trpc.apiKeys.list` returns `Partial<ApiKey>[]` (`server/supabase-adapter.ts:158`) — every field optional, `name: string`, and timestamps as ISO **strings**, not `Date`s. The local type was a stale duplicate that had drifted from the source of truth in three ways at once.

2. **TS2339** — `invoice.date` at the billing-history table. `getBillingHistory` returns `BillingHistory`, whose timestamp field is `createdAt` (`server/supabase-adapter.ts:104-114`); there is no `date`.

**The fix**

- Derived the card's prop type from the router instead of restating it, so it can't drift again:
  ```ts
  type ApiKeyListItem = inferRouterOutputs<AppRouter>["apiKeys"]["list"][number];
  type DisplayableApiKey = ApiKeyListItem & Required<Pick<ApiKeyListItem, "id" | "keyPrefix">>;
  ```
- Added a `isDisplayableApiKey` type guard and narrowed once in the page (`displayableKeys`), so the card keeps a non-optional `id`/`keyPrefix` contract — its delete/regenerate callbacks genuinely need a `number` id, and guarding inside the card would only have produced dead buttons.
- Made `createdAt` render conditionally, matching how `lastUsedAt` already handled absence.
- `invoice.date` → `invoice.createdAt`.

No suppressions, no `any`, no deleted code. All changes are confined to `UserDashboard.tsx`, which exports only a prop-less default component — nothing else in the tree consumes its types, so no other file's inference can shift.

**Verification I could not run:** `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` requires interactive approval on this host and no approver is present; the serena LSP diagnostics tool is likewise ungranted. So I have not observed a zero-error compiler run — the reasoning above is type-level analysis against the actual server definitions, not a green build. Please run the check to confirm.

One side artifact: the repo's routing gate refused all mutations until a routing receipt existed, so I wrote `build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json` as the hook's recovery instructions specified. Remove it if it isn't meant to persist.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# STOP-HOOK: the enforcement surface for capability exhaustion.
#
# This is the piece that was missing. The doctrine existed; nothing sat between
# a worker's `blocked` conclusion and the operator. A Stop hook CAN refuse to
# let the turn end (exit 2 feeds stderr back to the model), which makes it the
# only place a stopping rule can actually be load-bearing.
#
# It reads the transcript's final assistant message, and if that message
# concedes without recorded exhaustion evidence, it BLOCKS the stop and tells
# the worker to run the cross-surface enumeration first.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
GATE="$ROOT/build-os/motion/gate-stop.mjs"
[ -f "$GATE" ] || exit 0
command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
# stdin carries the Stop event JSON, including transcript_path.
# stderr is NOT suppressed: on a refusal it carries the entire recovery
# instruction back to the model. Swallowing it would refuse the stop without
# telling the worker why or what to do — a capability the worker cannot
# discover at the moment of refusal is functionally absent.
node "$GATE"

1	// THE CONTINUATION CONTROLLER.
2	//
3	// THE DEFECT IT FIXES: `task_completion_without_continuation`. The substrate
4	// treated
5	//     current task finished  ==>  session should stop
6	// as if the implication held. It does not. Finishing a unit of work is not a
7	// stop condition, and neither is a local commit awaiting a push grant.
8	//
9	// The observed incident: the forward-motion gate was built, proven, committed —
10	// and the session then reported "Nothing is running. Queue unchanged and
11	// unadvanced." while #50 sat runnable with its dependency satisfied. The
12	// capability-exhaustion gate was working; nothing asked the next question.
13	//
14	// EXECUTION AUTHORITY AND PUBLICATION AUTHORITY ARE DIFFERENT. An unpushed
15	// commit blocks publication, not work. Downstream work that does not require
16	// publication first proceeds locally, with the commit preserved.
17	
18	import { prioritise } from "./objective.mjs";
19	
20	export const TERMINAL_CONDITIONS = [
21	  "explicit_operator_stop",
22	  "no_remaining_queued_work",
23	  "all_remaining_blocked_after_exhaustion",
24	  "authority_or_safety_forbids_execution",
25	  "unavoidable_environment_termination",
26	];
27	
28	// Stated as a list because these were the two the substrate actually got wrong.
29	export const NON_TERMINAL = [
30	  "current_task_completed",
31	  "commit_awaiting_push_authorization",
32	];
33	
34	/**
35	 * @param {object} state
36	 *   tasks: [{ id, status, depends_on:[], requires_publication_of:[], blocked_evidence }]
37	 *   published_tips: []          — commits already pushed
38	 *   operator_stop: bool
39	 *   safety_stop: bool
40	 *   environment_terminating: bool
41	 *   transition_log: []          — prior attempts, for loop control
42	 */
43	export function continuationDecision(state = {}) {
44	  const tasks = state.tasks || [];
45	
46	  // `term` takes its evidence EXPLICITLY. It used to default to `evaluated`,
47	  // which is declared further down — so every early terminal path threw a
48	  // temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError instead of permitting the stop, and a
49	  // controller that throws on `operator_stop` is worse than no controller.
50	  // The same defect class was fixed once already in gate-recovery.mjs; a
51	  // default parameter referencing a later `const` is the shape to watch for.
52	  if (state.operator_stop === true)
53	    return term("explicit_operator_stop", "the operator issued a stop", []);
54	  if (state.safety_stop === true)
55	    return term("authority_or_safety_forbids_execution", "authority or safety policy forbids further execution", []);
56	  if (state.environment_terminating === true)
57	    return term("unavoidable_environment_termination", "the environment is terminating", []);
58	
59	  const open = tasks.filter((t) => t.status !== "completed" && t.status !== "deleted");
60	  if (open.length === 0)
61	    return term("no_remaining_queued_work", "the queue holds no open work", []);
62	
63	  // Runnable = every dependency completed, and any publication prerequisite
64	  // actually published. A task whose ONLY obstacle is an unpushed commit that
65	  // it does not itself require is still runnable.
66	  const completed = new Set(tasks.filter((t) => t.status === "completed").map((t) => t.id));
67	  const published = new Set(state.published_tips || []);
68	
69	  const evaluated = open.map((t) => {
70	    const unmetDeps = (t.depends_on || []).filter((d) => !completed.has(d));
71	    const unmetPub = (t.requires_publication_of || []).filter((c) => !published.has(c));
72	    const exhausted = t.blocked_evidence?.verdict === "concession_allowed";
73	    return {
74	      id: t.id, subject: t.subject,
75	      unmet_dependencies: unmetDeps,
76	      unmet_publication_prerequisites: unmetPub,
77	      genuinely_blocked: exhausted === true,
78	      runnable: unmetDeps.length === 0 && unmetPub.length === 0 && exhausted !== true,
79	    };
80	  });
81	
82	  const runnable = evaluated.filter((e) => e.runnable);
83	  const blockedNotExhausted = evaluated.filter((e) => !e.runnable && !e.genuinely_blocked);
84	
85	  if (runnable.length === 0) {
86	    // Every remaining task must have PASSED capability exhaustion before this
87	    // counts as terminal. "Nothing looks runnable to me" is not evidence.
88	    if (blockedNotExhausted.length > 0) {
89	      return {
90	        artifact: "continuation_decision",
91	        decision: "continue",
92	        next_task: null,
93	        reasons: [
94	          `no task is runnable, but ${blockedNotExhausted.length} have NOT passed capability exhaustion: ` +
95	          blockedNotExhausted.map((b) => b.id).join(", "),
96	          "run the concession gate on each before treating the queue as blocked",
97	        ],
98	        evaluated,
99	        binding: "STOP REFUSED — unexhausted blockers are not terminal.",
100	      };
101	    }
102	    return term("all_remaining_blocked_after_exhaustion",
103	      `every remaining task is genuinely blocked with recorded exhaustion evidence: ${evaluated.map((e) => e.id).join(", ")}`, evaluated);
104	  }
105	
106	  // LOOP CONTROL. Repeatedly selecting the same task without state changing is
107	  // not progress; escalate through exhaustion rather than cycling.
108	  const log = state.transition_log || [];
109	
110	  // VALUE ORDERING, not queue order. The controller used to take runnable[0] —
111	  // the next runnable task — which is why it could refuse to stop and still
112	  // spend four packets on an anchor migration that moved the objective by
113	  // nothing. Every step was correct; nothing asked whether the task was still
114	  // worth doing. Deferral here is a statement about ORDER, not validity.
115	  const ordered = prioritise(runnable.map((e) => ({ ...(tasks.find((t) => t.id === e.id) || {}), id: e.id })));
116	  const byValue = ordered.do_now.length
117	    ? runnable.filter((e) => ordered.do_now.includes(e.id))
118	    : runnable;
119	  const next = byValue[0] ?? runnable[0];
120	  const repeats = log.filter((l) => l.next_task === next.id && l.state_changed === false).length;
121	  if (repeats >= 2) {
122	    return {
123	      artifact: "continuation_decision",
124	      decision: "continue",
125	      next_task: runnable[1]?.id ?? null,
126	      reasons: [`task ${next.id} was selected ${repeats}x with no state change — escalating past it rather than looping`,
127	        runnable[1] ? `selecting ${runnable[1].id} instead` : "no alternative runnable task; run capability exhaustion on " + next.id],
128	      evaluated,
129	      binding: "STOP REFUSED — but the repeating task is escalated, not retried.",
130	    };
131	  }
132	
133	  return {
134	    artifact: "continuation_decision",
135	    decision: "continue",
136	    next_task: next.id,
137	    next_subject: next.subject,
138	    reasons: [
139	      `${runnable.length} runnable task(s); task completion is NOT a stop condition`,
140	      `selected ${next.id} — dependencies satisfied, no unmet publication prerequisite`,
141	      ordered.do_now.length
142	        ? `value gate: DO_NOW ${ordered.do_now.join(", ")}; DEFERRED ${ordered.deferred.join(", ") || "(none)"} — deferred work stays real, it is simply not next`
143	        : "value gate: NO runnable task serves an open exit criterion — the queue holds only deferrable debt, which is itself worth reporting",
144	    ],
145	    value_ordering: ordered,
146	    evaluated,
147	    binding: "STOP REFUSED — begin the next task.",
148	  };
149	
150	  function term(condition, why, ev) {
151	    return {
152	      artifact: "continuation_decision",
153	      decision: "stop",
154	      terminal_condition: condition,
155	      next_task: null,
156	      reasons: [why],
157	      evaluated: ev,
158	      binding: "Stop permitted: a registered terminal condition holds.",
159	    };
160	  }
161	}
